commit_message:
[json] Parser: Add more checks for fast-iterable keys

We didn't check all the required properties for fast iterable keys in
the JSON parser. Some of these properties are only relevenat for
JSON.stringify, but nevertheless need to be checked in the parser before
we mark a descriptor array as fast iterable.

findings.title: Missing return causes incorrect FastIterableState update when last JSON object key doesn't match feedback
findings.message: In `ParseJsonObjectProperties<FastIterableState::kUnknown>()`, when the last key of a JSON object does not match the feedback descriptor (i.e., `is_slow || !key_match` is true) and no comma follows (i.e., it is the final property), the code falls through to `++idx` instead of returning. This incorrectly increments the descriptor index, making `idx == descriptors_end` true after the `do...while` loop exits. The subsequent check `if (idx == descriptors_end)` then calls `descriptors->set_fast_iterable_if(FastIterableState::kJsonFast, FastIterableState::kUnknown)`, marking the descriptor array as fast-iterable even though the last key failed to satisfy the fast-iterable requirements. This stale marking causes a DCHECK failure in `IsFastKey(obj, no_gc)` in `json-stringifier.cc` when the stringifier attempts to use the fast path on a descriptor array that was incorrectly promoted to `kJsonFast`.
findings.suggestion: Add `return true;` inside the `if (V8_UNLIKELY(is_slow || !key_match))` block, after the inner `if (Check(JsonToken::COMMA))` block, so that when no comma follows the mismatched last key the function returns immediately without executing `++idx` and without triggering the incorrect fast-iterable state promotion.

ground_truth.root_cause: In commit 5fdab0114d1 (`[json] Parser: Add more checks for fast-iterable keys`), the `kJsonUnknown` branch of `ParseJsonObjectProperties` was restructured. The old code had an explicit `return true;` for the no-more-properties case after a mismatch, but the new code omitted it inside the `if (V8_UNLIKELY(is_slow || !key_match))` block. The `kJsonFast` branch (in the same function) correctly had `return true;` in the equivalent location, but the newly written `kJsonUnknown` branch did not, leaving `++idx` reachable when it should not be.
